newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain sends accused Qatari spies to jail.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain sends accused Qatari spies to jail.

text.p: Bahrain's State Security Court on Wednesday found a Qatari man and woman guilty of spying and sentenced them to three years in prison, a government official said.
"Two Qataris arrested for spying were sentenced to three years in prison each and were fined 1,000 dinars ($2,650) each by the court on Wednesday," he said.
The trial of Fahad Hamad Abdullah al-Baker and Salwa Jassim Mohammed Fakhri began on December 4. They were found guilty of gathering intelligence for the Qatari government, the official said.
Manama has said the two confessed to the charges before an investigating judge. Qatar denies the two were spies.
Qatar has accused Bahrain of torturing al-Baker and said the trial "set a dangerous precedent in Gulf ties". Bahrain denies the allegations.

The case has raised tensions between Bahrain and Qatar, already at odds because of a territorial dispute concerning a cluster of small islands and sandbanks in the Gulf controlled by Bahrain since the 1930s but also claimed by Qatar.
Qatar has taken the case over the islands to the International Court of Justice in The Hague. The move has angered Bahrain, which prefers a regional solution.
